summary: China sets 2030 targets for elder care and childcare as its population ages, Alibaba's AI cloud grows while online shopping slips, and US data show how many AI chips it let China buy.
body: On Monday China published targets for 2030 to expand care for older people and young children. Nursing-care beds are to make up 73% of beds in elderly-care homes, about 2,000 old public nursing homes will be renovated, and every prefecture-level city is to have childcare centres. Kindergartens are encouraged to take 2- and 3-year-olds, and employers to offer on-site childcare.[^1][^2] Background: China's population fell for a fourth year in 2025, births hit a record low, and earlier support has not reversed that, Reuters notes.[^1] For young Chinese, this touches both caring for parents and deciding whether to have children.

Alibaba, one of China's biggest tech firms, said its AI cloud revenue grew 53% last quarter, but its main online shopping business in China shrank 5%, which Reuters links to weak consumer spending and the property slump.[^3] Its CEO, Eddie Wu, said China's own computing chips are progressing "ahead of our original expectations", but warned that new US export rules "will affect next year's products and services".[^3] Its AI unit's losses tripled.[^4]

In the US, a House committee released data showing Washington approved exports of about 879,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD AI chips to Chinese firms between December 2025 and May 2026, out of 3.4 million requested. Critics in Congress question the review; Nvidia says the sales had "strict conditions" and that it has since stopped shipping those chips to China.[^5] Separately, the jobless rate for urban 16- to 24-year-olds not in school fell to 17.2% in October from 18% in September.[^6]
differences: On chips, US critics say the approvals were too generous, while Nvidia says they were limited and conditional.[^5] On births, Beijing presents the care plan as meeting public needs; Reuters notes past measures have not lifted the birth rate.[^1]
